risks.description: POST /approve can return 200 {"status":"approved"} from the in-memory view while the durable store still says pending — the UI/API and persistence disagree.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 approving an invoice records the approval durably

risks.description: Approval state may not survive a process restart: the service re-seeds/wipes the store on boot, so a previously approved invoice could read back as pending or vanish.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 approval state survives a re-read of persisted state

risks.description: The approve effect can land durably and then the response stalls past the client timeout, leaving the caller unable to tell whether the approval/payment happened.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 approving an invoice records the approval durably

risks.description: Two simultaneous approvals of the same invoice may each record a payment, double-paying under a race even though sequential idempotency might pass.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 approving an invoice records the approval durably

risks.description: An approval write could bleed into or mutate other invoices' persisted records rather than only the targeted invoice.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 approving an invoice records the approval durably

scenarios.title: API read says approved but durable store must agree
scenarios.purpose: Catch the case where /approve reports success and the in-memory GET reflects it, yet the durable store was never updated (UI/backend drift).
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a dedicated invoice id UICHK-1 that no other scenario touches; serialized on the shared store key so no concurrent boot/wipe interferes.
scenarios.rationale: An HTTP 200 and the process's in-memory view are not evidence of durability; the state.py oracle reads the file, so disagreement between the API response and the persisted record is directly observable.
expected_observations: Durable store (state.py) shows UICHK-1 status=approved with exactly one approval and one payment
forbidden_observations: state.py reports UICHK-1 status=pending after a 200 approve
state.py shows payments=0 while the API claims approved

scenarios.title: Approval survives a service restart / re-read of persisted state
scenarios.purpose: Verify a recorded approval is still present after the api process is restarted, exercising AC-APPROVAL-002 survival across a fresh read of the durable store.
scenarios.isolation_note: Restarts the shared api service and wipes the whole store; must run alone on the shared store key so it cannot clobber other scenarios' invoices.
scenarios.rationale: Boot logic can re-seed or unlink the store; the only trustworthy check is reading the durable file after the process has been recycled.
expected_observations: Before restart, durable store shows RSTRT-1 approved with one payment
After restart, durable store still shows RSTRT-1 approved with exactly one payment
forbidden_observations: After restart, RSTRT-1 reads back as pending
After restart, RSTRT-1 is absent or STORE MISSING

scenarios.title: Approve that times out client-side must have either not paid or paid exactly once
scenarios.purpose: Detect the ambiguous case where the approval effect lands durably but the response stalls past the client timeout, leaving the caller unsure what happened.
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated invoice id TMO-1; serialized on the shared store key.
scenarios.rationale: A correct implementation returns quickly; a stall past the client timeout with the effect already persisted is the defect. The durable store is the authoritative oracle regardless of whether the HTTP call returned, so the state_check — not the response — decides the verdict.
expected_observations: POST responds within the timeout with status approved
Durable store shows TMO-1 approved with exactly one payment
forbidden_observations: The approve effect is persisted only after a stall past the client's timeout (caller cannot confirm the outcome)
Durable store shows more than one payment for a single approve

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of one invoice pay exactly once
scenarios.purpose: Exercise a race: fire two /approve calls at the same invoice concurrently and confirm the durable store records only one payment.
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated invoice id RACE-1; the race is created inside the scenario via simultaneous requests, and it is serialized against other scenarios on the shared store key.
scenarios.rationale: Sequential idempotency passing does not guarantee race safety; simultaneous requests can each append a payment if the check-then-write is not atomic. This is distinct from the covered sequential double-approve.
expected_observations: Durable store shows RACE-1 approved with exactly one payment
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows two or more payments for RACE-1
RACE-1 records two approvals leading to a double pay

scenarios.title: Approving one invoice leaves other invoices untouched
scenarios.purpose: Confirm an approval writes only the targeted invoice's durable record and does not flip or create state on a sibling invoice.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses dedicated invoice ids ISOL-A and ISOL-B; serialized on the shared store key.
scenarios.rationale: A record write that mutates the whole store must not corrupt or approve invoices other than the target.
expected_observations: ISOL-A durable record shows approved with one payment
ISOL-B durable record remains pending with zero approvals and payments
forbidden_observations: ISOL-B becomes approved or gains a payment after approving ISOL-A

assumptions: The api service is started with PORT bound to 127.0.0.1:8955 and STORE pointing at the durable file that r5/fixture/state.py reads.
state.py accepts an invoice id as an extra argument to filter output (base approved command plus one arg), printing '<id> status=<s> approvals=<n> payments=<n>'.
Invoices are created on first touch, so dedicated invoice ids (UICHK-1, RSTRT-1, TMO-1, RACE-1, ISOL-A/B) are safe, run-scoped namespaces.
restart_service('api') recycles the same process the requests target, and the durable store path is stable across the restart.
unresolved_questions: Neither acceptance criterion states whether an approval must survive a full service restart, or only a re-read of the file within the same process lifetime; gen-w2-restart-survives assumes the stronger reading of AC-APPROVAL-002 — confirm intended durability scope.
No acceptance criterion covers authentication/authorization or an approval-required gate on /approve; if approvals must be actor-authorized, an AC is missing and cannot be verified as-is.
No criterion specifies handling of a missing or malformed actor/body (the service falls back to actor='unknown'); confirm whether that is intended or a requirement gap.
AC-APPROVAL-001 does not quantify the payment effect (one payment per approval); the idempotency/concurrency checks assume 'approved implies exactly one payment' — confirm this invariant is intended.
